x-maintenance: Hand-written and checked in, not generated: Hono registers routes as code and there is no decorator to read them off. That makes this file a promise rather than a derivation, so it has to be updated in the same change set as any route it describes - see CLAUDE.md. The rationale for every route is in docs/design/http-api.md; the operator's version is docs/guide/http-api.md. Where the three disagree, the design doc is the spec and this is the bug.

info.title: silo HTTP API
info.summary: The CRUD, media, transfer, plugin and administration API of a silo instance.
info.description:
JSON everywhere, under `/api`. There is no URL versioning (D13): a breaking
change is a release-note event tied to a binary upgrade, and the archive
format carries its own `format_version`. CORS is enabled for `/api/*`.

**Environment paths have two spellings.** Every path below written
`/environments` is also served at `/envs` — one handler registered twice, so
authorization cannot land on one spelling and miss the other. Only the
canonical `/environments` form is listed here; `/envs` behaves identically.

**Authentication** is a claims-based API key, presented as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-Api-Key: <key>`. There are no users,
sessions or cookies. Claims are deny-by-default. A collection whose schema
does not set `"x-silo-auth": true` is readable anonymously; once a key is
presented its claims become the visibility boundary, and even a public
collection then needs the matching read claim. The claim each operation asks
for is named in its description.

**Optimistic concurrency.** `PUT` and `DELETE` on an entry, and every plugin
mutation that writes a record, require the expected revision as
`If-Match: "3"` or `?rev=3`. A mismatch is `409`.

**Variables.** Every route that answers an entry substitutes `{{NAME}}` from
the environment's variables by default. `?variables=raw` answers the stored
text instead, for editors. Any other value is `400`.

servers.description: A local instance on the default listen address.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness, and who the presented key is.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: Projects and the environments inside them.

tags.name: Variables
tags.description: Names declared per project, valued per environment (D57).

tags.name: Collections
tags.description: Collection definitions and their JSON Schemas.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Full-text and filtered search at three reaches (D30).

tags.name: Media configuration
tags.description: Where the bytes go, where URLs point, what may be uploaded.

tags.name: Administration
tags.description: The audit trail, operating metrics and server settings.

get.description: The one route the auth middleware skips entirely. Never authenticated.

The label, display prefix and normalized claims of the key on this
request. The admin calls it to verify a key before saving a server.

prefix.description: The display prefix, e.g. `silo_ab12`. Empty under `--no-auth`.

get.description:
Visibility is per project: a key sees a project it holds a collection
claim for, and nothing else. Fixed claims such as `keys:read` deliberately
do not count. With no key, only projects holding a public collection.

200.description: The projects this caller may see.

post.description: Claim: `collections:{project}/*/*:create`.

schema.description: The id under any of three accepted spellings.

patch.description:
Claims are `collections:create` and `collections:delete` at
`{project}/*/*`, checked at **both** the old and the new name (D51).
The response says which claims were rewritten to follow the rename and
which changed reach without being rewritten.

200.description: What the rename did, or would do under `?dry_run=true`.

delete.description:
Refuses while content exists. `?force=true` erases every entry
underneath and additionally requires `entries:delete` at `{project}/*/*`
(D37).

get.description: Filtered by claim, the way the project listing is. Also served at `/envs`.

200.description: The environments this caller may see.

post.description: Claim: `collections:{project}/{env}/*:create`.

patch.description: Rename permissions at `{project}/{env}/*`, at both names (D51).

200.description: What the rename did, or would do.

delete.description:
Refuses while content exists. `?force=true` additionally requires
`entries:delete` at `{project}/{env}/*`.

post.summary: Copy another environment of this instance into this one
post.description:
Destination-driven: the path names the destination and the body names
the source (D22). No `transfer:*` claim, because this reaches no scope
the caller could not already read or write one entry at a time. It asks
for the read half across the source scope and the write half across the
destination; `replace` mode adds `entries:delete` and
`collections:delete` there. Touches no media.

200.description: What the copy did, or would do under `dry_run`.

post.summary: Declare a variable in the project
post.description:
Declaring reaches every environment in the project, so it asks for
`collections:{project}/*/*:create`. An initial `value` lands in `?env=`
and is additionally held to the value authority — `entries:update`
across that environment.

value.description: Optional initial value, for the `?env=` environment only.

patch.summary: Rename a declaration, or rewrite its description
patch.description:
A rename rewrites **no content**: every `{{OLD}}` already stored stays
as an unresolved reference, deliberately. A rename asks for
`collections:create` and `collections:delete` at `{project}/*/*`; a
description change asks for `create` alone.

delete.summary: Undeclare a variable, and every environment's value with it

get.summary: Every declaration in the project, with this environment's value
get.description:
Needs `entries:read` on **any** collection in the environment. That is
the honest floor: a value is substituted into every entry that
references it, so anyone who can read one entry can already see it.

200.description: The declarations, valued for this environment.

put.description:
Every other environment's is untouched. Changing one value rewrites what
every entry in this environment answers, so it asks for
`collections:{project}/{env}/*:entries:update`.

value.description: May be empty, which is a value somebody chose.

delete.summary: Clear this environment's value, leaving the name declared
delete.description: Authorized as an update, not a delete: the declaration survives.

get.description:
Summaries, and no schema (D54) — a schema is the largest thing a
collection carries and the one thing a list of them never draws. Each
item is filtered by `collections:schema:read`, or by the collection
being public when no key is presented.

200.description: The collections this caller may see.

post.description: Claim: `collections:{project}/{env}/{name}:create`.

get.description:
For the callers that genuinely read across all of them — a form
resolving `silo://` refs, a client validating without a round trip per
type. A sibling of `collections` rather than a path beneath it, because
`schemas` is a legal collection name.

200.description: Every collection with its stored schema, claim-filtered.

get.description:
Filter, sort and paginate with the query grammar below. Public without a
key unless the schema sets `"x-silo-auth": true`; with a key, needs
`collections:...:entries:read`.

post.description:
The body is the entry's own fields. `id`, `rev`, `created_at` and
`updated_at` are the envelope and are written by the server. Claim:
`collections:...:entries:create`.

patch.description:
Distinct from the other two renames in one way: `$ref`s address
collections by name, so this rewrites every referring schema as well,
and asks for `collections:schema:update` on each of them up front (D51).

200.description: What the rename did, or would do.

get.description:
Bundled on the way out (D54): every referenced collection's schema is
re-resolved into `$defs` as it stands now, so one schema is a document a
client can render on its own.

200.description: The collection and its bundled schema.

put.description:
Claim: `collections:...:schema:update`. Turning `x-silo-auth` on or off
additionally requires `collections:...:access:update`.

delete.description:
Refuses while entries exist. `?force=true` erases them and additionally
requires `entries:delete` on the collection (D37).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The entry id. A ULID for anything silo created; an imported id may be anything.

put.description:
A full replace, not a patch. Requires the expected revision as
`If-Match: "<rev>"` or `?rev=<rev>`. Claim:
`collections:...:entries:update`.

409.description: The stored revision is not the expected one.

delete.description: Requires the expected revision, like `PUT`. Claim `entries:delete`.

get.description:
The reach is in the path, not a query parameter: a missing `?project=`
would silently widen a search (D30). Results are bounded to the targets
the caller may read.

post.description:
Reads every entry in the instance, so it asks for the same instance-wide
read authority an export does: `collections:schema:read` and
`collections:entries:read` at `*/*/*`.

200.description: What was rebuilt, plus an integrity check.

get.summary: Export the whole instance as a tar.gz
get.description:
Streamed, not buffered — an archive carries the whole media library.
Claims: `transfer:export`, plus `collections:schema:read` and
`collections:entries:read` at `*/*/*`. `?with_keys=true` additionally
requires `keys:export`.

parameters.name: with_keys
parameters.description: Include the `_keys` collection in the archive.

post.description:
The body is either the raw archive or a `multipart/form-data` `file`
part. Both are streamed. Claims: `transfer:import`, `media:create`, and
`collections:*` write permissions at `*/*/*`. `?mode=replace` adds
`collections:delete`, `entries:delete` and `media:delete`. An archive
carrying keys additionally needs `keys:import`, and loads without them
when the caller does not hold it.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: `replace` drops each archived collection before writing it back.

parameters.name: validate
parameters.description: Validate every entry against its schema as it loads.

parameters.name: prefer
parameters.description: Which side wins on a conflict.

post.summary: Pull another silo's archive and import it
post.description:
Streamed end to end: the source streams its export and this loads from
that stream. Claims: `transfer:copy`, `media:create` and instance-wide
write permissions; `replace` mode and `with_keys` add the same claims
`POST /api/import` asks for.

get.description: Claim: `keys:read`. The secret is never in a listing.

post.description:
Claim: `keys:create`, and every requested claim must already be covered
by the caller's — minting never widens. The plaintext secret is in this
response and nowhere else, ever.

201.description: The new key, including its secret.

key.description: The plaintext secret. Returned exactly once.

patch.summary: Edit a key's label and claims
patch.description:
`claims` replaces the list outright rather than merging, because a merge
cannot express removing a claim. Gated on `keys:create` and bounded by
two delegation checks: against the target's current claims and against
the requested ones (D63). `hash`, `prefix`, `owner` and `parent_id` are
unreachable. A managed plugin key is refused.

delete.summary: Revoke a key, and everything descended from it
delete.description:
Claim: `keys:revoke`, and the authority to have minted the target — if
you could not mint a key this powerful, you may not destroy one (D37).
Descendants go with it (D38); `GET /api/audit` names what went.

get.description: No claim (D58). Reading the library needs none.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Substring match on the display filename.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Exact folder, or everything beneath it with `recursive`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Substring match on the content type, e.g. `image/`.

post.description:
Claim: `media:create`. The extension is checked against the library's
allowlist, not the declared content type.

folder.description: Normalised `/a/b`. Omit for the library root.

post.description:
Always `200`: the request itself succeeded, and each id's outcome is
data in the body — including the referrers a `409` could not carry.
Claim: `media:delete`; `force` additionally requires `entries:update`
and `entries:read` at every scope the assets are referenced from (D49).

Claims: `media:delete` **and** `media:purge`, which no preset but `root`
carries — on `media:delete` alone every integration key that manages its
own uploads could empty the instance's library in one request (D65).
There is no undo, hence the typed confirmation.

200.description: Per-id outcomes, plus how many folder records went.

post.description:
Adopts blobs with no record, finishes an interrupted deletion, aborts
one that cannot finish, and reports orphans without deleting them.
Claims: `media:create` and `media:delete`.

get.summary: Every distinct extension in the library
get.description: No claim (D55, D58). Feeds the admin's Type filter.
No claim. Folders that exist because someone made them.

post.description: Claim: `media:create`.

patch.description:
Carries every asset and descendant folder with it. Refuses on collision
unless `merge: true`. A body rather than a path parameter, because a
folder path contains `/`. Claim: `media:create`.

200.description: The normalised paths the move used.

delete.description:
Empty only by default. `?recursive=true` takes everything inside it and
answers `200` with per-id outcomes instead of `204`. `?force=true`
requires `recursive` and the content authority a forced asset delete
needs. Claim: `media:delete`.

folders_deleted.description: 0 when an asset survived, since the folder is then not gone.

get.summary: Where the library keeps its bytes
get.description:
Claim: `media:configure` — one claim rather than a read/write pair,
because the read names the bucket, endpoint and access key id (D45). The
secret never leaves.

200.description: The file's configuration and the one in force.

put.description:
A whole configuration, not a patch. `secret_access_key` is the
exception the read forces: absent keeps the file's value, `""` clears it.

get.summary: Where media URLs point, and what may be uploaded
get.description: Claim: `media:configure` (D46).

200.description: The `[media]` table, as the file holds it and as it is in force.

put.description:
A whole table, not a patch: nothing here is write-only, so an omitted
field means cleared rather than kept.

base_url.description: `""` puts media URLs back on the store's own public root.

get.description: No claim.

patch.summary: Rename, move or retag an asset
patch.description:
Claim: `media:create` — the claim that already governs putting a file
into the library. None of this changes what a reference resolves to,
which is what separates it from a replace.

delete.description:
Refuses while anything references it, with the referrers the caller may
read in the body. `?force=true` deletes anyway and additionally requires
`entries:read` and `entries:update` at every referring scope (D49).
Claim: `media:delete`.

500.description: The record was staged for deletion but the blob delete did not finish.

get.description:
No claim to read, but the rows are filtered by what the caller may see:
`total` is the true count and `visible` is how many of them this key may
read (D58). An anonymous caller enumerates nothing.

total.description: Every referrer, whether or not this caller may see it.

visible.description: How many of them this caller may read.

visible_capped.description: True when the visibility scan hit its row cap.

post.description:
Keeps the id, the URL and every reference to it (D67). Claim:
`media:replace` — not `media:create`, which the `write` preset carries,
so gating on it would let every upload key overwrite anybody else's
file — **and** `entries:read`/`entries:update` at every referring scope.

200.description: The asset, with new bytes behind the same id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The catalog id, so the URL survives a rename. A pre-D23 blob key still resolves.

get.description:
Outside `/api`, outside the auth middleware, and not authenticated.
Carries an `ETag` of the content hash and answers `304` to a matching
`If-None-Match`. Cached for an hour and deliberately not `immutable`,
because what an id points at can be replaced.

400.description: The identifier contained a path separator.

get.description:
Answers with every section at once, because the page shows them together
and four round trips to draw one screen is four ways for it to be
half-drawn. Claim: `settings:configure` — one claim, not a pair, because
the read names the data directory, the log path, and whether
authentication is on at all (D47).

200.description: Every section, plus whether the file can be written.

parameters.name: table

put.description:
One table at a time, because they are separate tables with separate
failure modes and a rejected `[search]` value must not stop a `[log]`
level being fixed. A whole document rather than a patch; an unknown key
is refused rather than dropped. Claim: `settings:configure`.

schema.description: The table's fields, as `GET /api/settings` describes them.

get.description:
What each package requested, what it was granted, what it is actually
doing, and the author's reason for every claim. Claim: `plugins:read`.

200.description: Every plugin with a record on this instance.

post.summary: Install a package and adopt it
post.description:
No restart and no shell (D42). A JSON body names a spec; a multipart
body may carry a `.tgz` instead, up to 64 MiB, which takes the identical
path through the installer. Claim: `plugins:enable` — the claim that
already decides whether plugin code runs. The `[[plugins]]` block this
writes carries **no** claims: authority stays in the record, where the
delegation checks and the audit trail can see it.

file.description: A package tarball. Omit it and send `spec` instead.

claims.description: Comma-separated, unlike the JSON body's array.

201.description:
The plugin's view, plus any warnings. A package contributing only
providers has no record to view, so `state` and `runtime` are `null`.

500.description: The package on disk cannot start.

post.summary: Re-read silo.toml and make the running set match it
post.description:
Reports per plugin rather than refusing over one: a rescan that refused
would abandon every other change in the file. Claim: `plugins:enable`.
Writes no record, so no `If-Match`.

200.description: What started, restarted, stopped, was skipped or failed.

get.description: Carries `ETag: "<rev>"` to send back as `If-Match`. Claim `plugins:read`.

delete.summary: Take a plugin off this instance
delete.description:
Unlists it, destroys its record, stops its worker and removes the
package (D43). Claim: `plugins:enable`, the same claim install takes,
because it is the same decision read the other way round. `If-Match` is
required wherever there is a record to demand it about — a
provider-only install has none.

get.description:
Answered as **JSON**, never as a document, with `nosniff`,
`default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `no-store` (D41). This origin also
serves the admin SPA, which keeps an API key per configured server in
`localStorage`, so a plugin's HTML rendered here would be a
credential-exfiltration primitive. Only the admin makes it a document,
inside a sandboxed iframe with no origin of its own. Claim
`plugins:read`.

entry.description: The file it came from, relative to the package.

put.description:
The body is the **complete** granted set, so sending it twice grants the
same thing. An omitted `claims` approves everything the package says it
**requires** — not everything it requested, which would make the word
optional mean nothing. Claim: `plugins:grant`, `If-Match` required:
approving means approving what you read, and a package whose request
changed in between is exactly the substitution the fence catches.

delete.description:
Clears the record's half only. Claims declared in `silo.toml` are the
other half and stay — `config_claims` on the view says what they are.
Claim: `plugins:grant`, `If-Match` required.

post.description:
Claim: `plugins:enable`, `If-Match` required. The response carries
`runtime`, which says what actually happened — it replaced
`restart_required` (D39).

Not `plugins:grant`: withdrawing authority and refusing to load are
separate remedies, and an operator who had to re-approve after every
pause would learn to approve widely. Claim: `plugins:enable`,
`If-Match` required.

patch.description:
An [RFC 7396](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7396) merge patch, so
one setting can change without restating the block and `null` removes
one. Claim: `plugins:configure`, `If-Match` required.

delete.summary: Clear the override and return to silo.toml's block
delete.description: The only way out of the pin an override creates. Claim `plugins:configure`.

post.summary: Tear the worker down and bring it back
post.description:
A plugin that missed its dispatch budget or crashed is not respawned on
its own. Claim: `plugins:enable`. Writes no record, so no `If-Match`.

200.description: What the plugin is doing now.

/api/ext/{name}/{path}.description:
One handler matches every plugin route (D36). A plugin's routes are data
the host interprets rather than patterns it registers, so a plugin can
neither shadow nor reorder anything in this file, and the set is resolved
per request — enable, disable, revoke and rescan apply to routes as they
do to hooks.

**A handler runs with the plugin's authority, not the caller's.** That is
why exposure is a claim (`http:route`) and why a route declaring
`auth: "public"` is called out separately: it publishes whatever the
plugin was granted at a URL anyone can reach. The caller's
`Authorization`, `X-Api-Key` and `Cookie` are withheld from the handler,
which receives an id, a label and claims instead.

Status, headers and body are the plugin's. A thrown validation or
authorization error maps to 400 or 403 through the same handler as
everything else, and a body past the route's declared limit is refused
rather than truncated.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
The rest of the path, matched against the routes the plugin's manifest
declares. Not URL-decoded before splitting, so a `%2F` inside a
parameter cannot become a separator. A bare `/api/ext/{name}`
addresses the plugin's root, which is `/`.

head.description: Reaches a declared `GET`; the content it produced is dropped here.

get.description:
Newest first. Read-only, and there is no route to write one: an event is
appended by the service that made the change, so an actor cannot claim
something happened that did not (D38). There is no delete either, which
is why `audit:read` has no `audit:write` beside it. Claim: `audit:read`.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Filter to one key id or plugin name.

get.summary: One bounded snapshot of this process
get.description:
Aggregate, low-cardinality operating facts only. Requests are grouped by
the registered route pattern, never by the requested path; query
strings, parameters, caller identities, bodies, credentials, content and
filesystem paths never enter the accumulator, so granting this does not
quietly become a content-read capability (D52). Claim
`observability:read`.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: The same secret, for callers that cannot set `Authorization`.

Project.name: project
Project.description: The project name, not its id.

Env.name: env
Env.description: The environment name. Also served under `/envs/{env}`.

Force.name: force
Force.description:
A second operation, not a modifier (D37). Only the literal string
`true` opts in, and it always asks for additional claims.

DryRun.name: dry_run
DryRun.description: Answer with what would change, and write nothing.

ExpectedId.name: expected_id
ExpectedId.description:
Bind the rename to the record's id, so a request delayed in flight
cannot rename whatever took the name in the meantime. A mismatch is 409.

VariableEnv.name: env
VariableEnv.description: Which environment an initial value lands in. Defaults to the default environment.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The expected revision, quoted. `?rev=` is the alternative.

Rev.name: rev
Rev.description: The expected revision, for callers that cannot set `If-Match`.

Filter.name: filter
Filter.description:
A URL-encoded JSON `Filter` document — see the `Filter` schema for its
grammar. Capped at 50 nodes and 10 levels of nesting.

Sort.name: sort
Sort.description:
Comma-separated RFC 9535 paths over the API response shape, each
optionally prefixed with `-` for descending, e.g.
`-$.updated_at,$.data.title`. A wildcard path is refused: it selects
many nodes and has no deterministic order.

Variables.name: variables
Variables.description:
`resolved` substitutes `{{NAME}}` from the environment's variables.
`raw` answers the stored text, which is what an editor wants — a form
seeded with a resolved value saves that value back and replaces the
reference with a snapshot of it. Any other value is a 400.

SearchQuery.name: q
SearchQuery.description: The text to match. Omit it to filter and sort without a term.

ValidationFailed.description: The request was malformed, or an entry failed its schema.

Unauthorized.description: No key was presented, or the presented key is not valid.

Forbidden.description: The key is missing a claim this operation needs.

Conflict.description:
The write would collide: a revision mismatch, a name already taken, or a
delete refused while content exists.

PluginRouteResponse.description:
Whatever the plugin answers, plus the host's own refusals: 403 when
`http:route` is not granted, 404 when no plugin serves this path (which
is also the answer for a plugin that is absent, ungranted or disabled —
that is the operator's business, not a caller's), 405 when it serves the
path but not this method, and 504 when the worker did not answer inside
its `timeout_ms`, naming `POST /api/plugins/{name}/restart` as the
remedy.

ScopeName.description: Lowercase letter first, then `[a-z0-9_-]`, at most 64 characters.

id.description: The record's ULID. Stable across renames (D51).

RenamePreview.description:
What a rename did, or would do. The interesting part is the two claim
lists: a literal claim segment is a reference and is rewritten, while a
wildcard or prefix pattern is a pattern over names and never is — so the
second list is the only place anything says a key's reach moved without
its claims changing (D51, D64).

value.description:
**This** environment's value. `null` means the project declares the
name and this environment has given it nothing, which is distinct
from `""` — a value somebody chose.

set_in.description:
How many of the project's environments have a value, so a page can
say "set in 2 of 3" without learning any other environment's value.

JsonSchema.description:
A JSON Schema document. silo adds two vocabulary extensions:
`x-silo-auth: true` on the root makes the collection non-public, and a
`silo://` `$ref` addresses another collection in the same scope, which
the server bundles into `$defs` on the way out.

CollectionSummary.description: What a listing answers — everything a navigation surface draws, and no schema (D54).

requires_auth.description: Whether reading it needs a key (`x-silo-auth`).

Entry.description:
The entry's own fields, plus the envelope. `rev` is in the response
because `PUT` and `DELETE` require it back as `If-Match`; the rest of
the envelope — the collection, the sequence, the scope — stays hidden.

Filter.description:
One node of the query AST (D29). Leaf ops address the virtual entry
document with an RFC 9535 path; group ops combine completed predicates.

value.description: Leaf ops except `exists`. An array for `in`.

SearchEngine.description: `scan` means there is no index, so the answer may be truncated.

SearchSnippet.description:
Three plain strings rather than one with markers in it: a body
containing a literal bracket would give a highlighter two candidate
pairs and no way to tell which the engine meant.

path.description: The path of the node the match came from.

before.description: Starts with an ellipsis when the fragment was cut.

match.description: The matched run, quoted from the original text.

total.description: Exact for what was visited. See `truncated`.

truncated.description:
True when a scan stopped at its visit cap or time budget, so `total`
counts what was examined rather than what exists.

index.description: "ok", or the message the index's own integrity check raised.

orphanDocuments.description: Index documents whose entry has gone.

ScopeCopyPreview.description: A bounded detail page, present only on a scope-copy dry run that asked for one.

id.description: Omitted when the caller may not read the destination scope.

selection.description:
Omit to copy the whole source scope. An item without `entry_ids`
copies its whole collection. An entry subset cannot be used with
`replace`.

source_api_key.description: A key on the source holding `transfer:export`.

Key.description: The public shape of a key record. Never the secret.

updated_at.description:
Equal to `created_at` until someone edits the label or the claims,
which is the only thing that moves it (D63).

owner.description:
Present only on a key silo minted for a plugin, so a listing can say
why this one is not an operator's to revoke (D34).

parent_id.description:
The key that minted this one. Revoking a key takes everything naming
it here, transitively (D38).

url.description:
Derived, not stored: it addresses the asset by catalog id, so it
survives a rename or a move.

folder.description: `""` for the library root, else a normalised `/a/b` path.

hash.description: sha256 of the bytes, hex. Also the `ETag` on the public stream.

state.description:
`deleting` means the blob delete has been committed to but may not
have finished. New references are refused and startup retries it.

usage_count.description: Present only where the caller asked for it, since counting is a query.

path.description: Normalised `/a/b`; never `""`, since the root needs no record.

MediaUsage.description: One entry's reference to one asset.

media_id.description: The catalog id, or `blob:<key>` for a pre-D23 reference.

MediaDeleteBatch.description:
The per-id outcomes every route that deletes many assets answers with,
so a bulk delete, a recursive folder delete and a purge report the same
shape (D49).

usage_count.description: On `media_in_use`: every referrer, visible or not.

MediaInUseError.description:
The 409 a guarded single delete answers with. The counts are the true
totals and the rows are only what this key may read: checking against
the true reach must not become the one place that discloses it.

adopted.description: Catalog records created for blobs that had none.

pruned.description: Assets whose blob is gone, so the record was dropped.

aborted.description: Assets returned to `active` because the blob delete failed again.

pending.description: Still staged after this pass — the delete failed and the abort could not be recorded either.

orphans.description: Blob keys no catalog record claims. Reported, never deleted.

SettingsOverride.description:
One field the file does not decide. A file is the third thing consulted
— flags outrank `SILO_*` variables, which outrank it — so without this,
an operator would type a bucket into a form, watch it save, and see the
instance keep using another one.

field.description: The field as this API spells it: `bucket`, `path`, `access_key_id`, ...

env.description:
The variable in force, when one is. Absent means something else
supplies the field — a flag, or a `silo.toml` edited by hand since
this process started.

MediaStorageFacts.description:
One media storage configuration, read out. There is no
`secret_access_key` and there will not be one: `secret_access_key_set`
is as much as a form needs to render "configured, leave blank to keep",
and everything more is handing a credential back out over the API it was
configured through.

secret_access_key_set.description: That a credential is configured, never the credential.

MediaStorageView.description:
Two configurations, not one, and the split is the design: `file` is what
the form edits and writes, `in_force` is what the instance is actually
doing, and they differ whenever a flag or a `SILO_*` variable outranks
the file (D45).

drivers.description: Every blob driver this process can open, plugin-contributed ones included.

config_path.description: Absent when this process was handed no config file.

read_only_reason.description: Why a save cannot land, when one cannot.

secret_access_key.description:
The one field that is not "a PUT of what was read": absent keeps
what the file holds, `""` clears it.

file.description: What the file names, and only that.

in_force.description: The same, after env vars and flags.

default_extensions.description: What a new instance starts with, so the page can offer it back.

ConfigField.description:
One setting's spec, sent to the admin so a new setting appears on the
page without the admin being taught about it separately.

env.description: The `SILO_*` variable that outranks the file for this field.

restart.description: Whether a change takes effect only at the next start.

writable.description: False for `[storage]`, which is reported and never written.
False when there is no config file, or it is not writable by this process.

restart_pending.description: True while any saved field is waiting for a restart.

PluginStatus.description:
What a plugin is **doing**, as distinct from what the record says about
it. The two can disagree: a granted, enabled plugin whose worker died on
a dispatch timeout is not running (D39).

state.description:
`stopped` is nobody's fault — disabled, or not listed in
`silo.toml`. `failed` is a crash or a dispatch that outlived its
budget; the restart route is the way back.

detail.description: Why it is not running, in a sentence, or `null` when it is.

PluginContributions.description: Everything a package contributes, declared in its manifest rather than discovered.

Plugin.description:
One plugin, as the management API reports it. The claim lists are the
load-bearing part: effective authority is the union of the record's
grant and what `silo.toml` declares, and `DELETE .../grant` clears only
the first (D40).

state.description: The resolver's answer, not the record's.

enabled.description: Explicit on the wire — a client reading `undefined` as false would show every plugin as off.

required.description: The subset of `requested` the package cannot work without, and what a bodyless grant approves.

granted.description: What the operator approved through the record — the half this API can change.

effective.description: The two of them together — what the plugin actually holds.

not_granted.description:
`requested` minus `effective`, computed here rather than left to the
client, which would be a second implementation of the wildcard-aware
comparison this repo keeps in one place.

key_id.description: The managed key carrying the grant. Its id only; the secret is host-side.

rev.description: Send back as `If-Match` on a change.

config_source.description: Which of the two sources won. An override makes the file's block stop applying.

reasons.description: Claim to the author's reason for wanting it. Documentation, from the manifest.

config_schema.description: JSON Schema for the config block. `null` means the plugin takes no configuration.

spec.description: An npm spec, a URL, a git remote, a local directory or a tarball path.

integrity.description: A subresource-integrity digest the fetched package must match.

claims.description:
Absent means absent, not empty: "grant nothing" and "grant what the
package requires" are different requests.

withdrawn.description: What the record held at the moment it went.

unlisted.description: Whether an entry was taken out of `silo.toml`.

removed.description: Whether the package left the data directory.

restarted.description: Torn down and started again because something it was started with changed.

order.description: The dispatch order after the rescan, which is the file's order.

AuditEvent.description:
One recorded **authority** change (D38). Entry writes are not audited —
`rev`, `updated_at` and the hook stream already are that, and
duplicating content history here would turn a log about decisions into a
log about traffic.

kind.description:
`cli` carries no id on purpose: the offline commands are bounded
by filesystem access, not by a key, so there is nothing to name.

id.description: The key record's id, for `kind: "key"` only. Survives revocation.

label.description: The key's label at the time, so a revoked key's entries stay readable.

subject.description: A key id for `key.*`, a plugin name for `plugin.*`, a table for `settings.configure`.

detail.description:
Everything action-specific, and never a secret or a hash. Claims
themselves are in: a trail that says the grant changed without
saying to what is a notification, not a record.

internal.description: Requests a plugin dispatched in-process rather than ones that crossed a socket.

latency.description: Percentiles are bucket upper bounds clamped to the slowest request observed.

endpoints.description:
The busiest 25, keyed by the **registered route pattern** so no
id or query string becomes a series. Endpoints collapse into one
`* <other>` row past 256.

timeline.description: One bucket per minute, pruned to the last sixty.

storage.description:
Cached background probes, so a snapshot never waits on a scan. The
walks follow no symlink and stop after 50,000 entries; the data
figure skips the media subtree, so the two are disjoint. A remote
provider's capacity is `null`, not guessed.

truncated.description: True when the walk hit its entry budget.

Error.description:
Every refusal takes this shape. `details` on a `validation_failed`
carries the validator's JSON Pointer paths.

details.description:
Validation pointers, the referrers of a refused media delete, or
the plugin and the remedy for a plugin failure.
